gbm_population_evidence.quote: Monocyte Antigen Carrier Cells for Newly Diagnosed GBM
Newly diagnosed glioblastoma patient with definitive resection prior to enrollment

candidate_evidence.quote: The investigational vaccine (MT-201-GBM) in this study is made from a type of immune cell called monocytes, which have been engineered to express a cytomegalovirus (CMV) protein.
monocytes isolated from patient's leukapheresis loaded with CMV pp65-LAMP (Lysosomal-associated Membrane Protein) mRNA (Messenger Ribonucleic Acid)

treatment_setting_evidence.quote: patients newly diagnosed with a type of brain tumor called glioblastoma (GBM)

role_evidence.quote: The monocyte vaccines are made from the patient's own cells, which are collected through a procedure called leukapheresis.

agents.drug_class_hint: autologous monocyte cell vaccine loaded with CMV pp65-LAMP mRNA (cell therapy / cancer vaccine)

role_evidence.quote: Patients will receive a total of 3 intravenous vaccines every 4 weeks after completing standard radiation therapy (XRT) and temozolomide (TMZ) and a single course of dose-intensified TMZ.

source_quote.quote: MGMT promoter unmethylated (Determined by Caris Life Science pyrosequencing);

coder_notes: Only investigational product is an autologous monocyte vaccine (excluded intervention type). Temozolomide is standard chemoradiation plus one dose-intensified TMZ cycle preceding the vaccine; coded soc_backbone (dose-intensified cycle not framed as the investigational question). Regimen coded not_applicable because there is no candidate agent. Gadolinium mentioned only in an exclusion criterion (allergy), not as an intervention. CMV pp65 is the vaccine antigen, not recorded as a tumour biomarker.
